title: RBI's Proposed Digital Payment Safeguards: Explained

faq.q: What is the primary goal of these proposed RBI safeguards?
faq.a: The primary goal is to enhance the security of digital payments and empower customers with greater control over their financial transactions, thereby reducing the incidence and impact of fraud.

faq.q: Will these features be mandatory for all banks?
faq.a: Once these proposals are finalised and issued as guidelines, they are generally mandatory for all regulated entities like banks and payment system operators to implement, ensuring uniform security standards across the ecosystem.

faq.q: When are these changes expected to be implemented?
faq.a: As these are currently proposals or draft rules, a definitive timeline for implementation is not yet available. They will typically go through a consultation process before being finalised and rolled out by banks.

faq.q: Can I set different limits for different payment methods?
faq.a: Yes, the proposals suggest that customers will have the flexibility to set distinct transaction and daily limits for various payment instruments like UPI, debit cards, and credit cards, tailored to their individual needs.

faq.q: How will I access these controls?
faq.a: It is expected that these controls will be accessible through your bank's official mobile banking application, internet banking portal, or potentially through dedicated customer service channels.

faq.q: Will these features apply to international transactions?
faq.a: While the primary focus is on domestic digital payments, the card on/off switch and limit settings could potentially extend to international transactions made using your debit or credit cards, depending on the final guidelines issued by the RBI.
